transcript.text: One of the outlets in my kitchen sparked and now half the kitchen has no power.

That sounds scary. I'm glad you're okay. Here's what to do for safety right now:

- Don't plug anything into that outlet or touch it. Unplug anything that's in it only if the plug isn't scorched or hot.
- If you smell burning, see smoke, or the outlet or wall feels warm, get everyone out and call 911.
- Check your electrical panel. A tripped breaker or a GFCI outlet that has "popped" is likely why half the kitchen lost power. Don't reset it yet. Leave that circuit off until an electrician has looked at the outlet. If the breaker didn't trip and the outlet still looks live, turn that breaker off if you can safely reach the panel. Don't do this if there's water near the panel.

I'll find a licensed electrician near you. Two quick questions:
1. What's your ZIP code?
2. Do you see any scorch marks or melting on the outlet, or smell burning?

ZIP is 94087. No burning smell now, but there's a faint dark mark around one of the slots. The breaker tripped yesterday evening and I tried resetting it a couple times but it trips right away, so I've left it off.

Good call leaving that breaker off. A breaker that trips again as soon as you reset it usually means there's a short on that circuit, and the dark mark points to that outlet as the likely spot. It isn't something to keep resetting. With the circuit off you're safe for now, but you'll want an electrician in the next day or so.

Here are electricians near Sunnyvale 94087:

1. Flores Electric, 408-899-8450. The closest at about 4.3 km away, in Santa Clara.
2. WCI Electric, 408-242-2069. About 4.9 km away, open Mon–Fri 8am–5pm.
3. University Electric, 408 496 0500. A bit farther at about 7.3 km, also in Santa Clara.

My listings don't include ratings or after-hours availability, so I picked Flores Electric as the top choice because it's closest.

Want me to send your request to Flores Electric so they call you back? If so, please send me:
- Your full name, best phone number, and email (email is optional)
- The service address with city, state and ZIP
- When someone can be there
- Whether you own or rent, and the type of home (house, condo, townhouse, etc.)
Before I send all that, why do you need to know whether I own or rent? And will Flores Electric get my email too, or just my phone number?

Both fair questions.

Why owner vs. renter: if you rent, the landlord or property manager usually has to approve electrical work and is often the one who pays. Your lease may also say repairs have to go through them. The electrician wants to know that up front so they don't show up and then can't start. If you rent, it's worth giving your landlord a heads-up too. Property type helps them plan access and any permit needs. You don't have to answer either one; I can mark them as unknown.

Your email: Flores Electric only gets what you give me. Email is optional. If you leave it out, they just get your name, phone number, the service address and the job details. If you do include it, it goes to them along with the rest. Before anything is sent, I'll confirm exactly what's being shared and ask for your okay.

Do you agree to share this information with Flores Electric so they can contact you about this job? A simple yes is fine. Also, would you prefer they call, text, or email?
Yes, that all looks right, go ahead and send it. One small detail: it's the outlet right next to the toaster. A call is best, or a text if they can't reach me.
